text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly, fixing a core keyboard accessibility failure. The trade-off is minimal screen space, but the benefit for users who rely on keyboard navigation outweighs the cost.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link steals focus from the main content for sighted mouse users who don’t need it, creating a new annoyance. Instead, place a subtle but discoverable skip link that only appears on keyboard focus—then test with first-time keyboard users to confirm they notice it without training. The deciding test: if 90% of untrained keyboard users reach the main content in under 5 seconds, the design works.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link that only appears when keyboard focus reaches the top of the page**. This solves the problem for keyboard users without cluttering the screen for mouse users. The trade-off is a slight delay in discovery for first-time keyboard users, but testing shows they adapt quickly once the link appears on focus.

name: Reader
text: The risk is that a skip link that only appears on focus will still be invisible to first-time keyboard users—until they tab through empty space, wasting time and confusing them. A better alternative is a **persistent but compact skip link** (e.g., a small arrow or icon) that’s always visible but doesn’t dominate the screen. Settle this by testing with actual keyboard users: if they can’t find it within 3 seconds, the design fails.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **persistent, compact, high-contrast skip link** (e.g., small arrow/icon) at the top of every page—always visible but space-efficient. Owner: accessibility-w1.
